citations.title: License Requirements
citations.requirement: Facility may not represent any service beyond its license (1). Capacity changes need prior AHCA Central Office approval (2). Converting uninspected space to resident use needs prior Field Office approval (3). Buildings under one license must be on contiguous property (4). Copies of annual fire and sanitation inspections go to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days (5). Facility must identify state-funded residents on request (6).

citations.title: Admission Procedures, Appropriateness of Placement and Continued Residency Criteria
citations.requirement: (1) Admission criteria, including age 18+, no stage 3-4 pressure sores, not bedridden except hospice, and the listed nursing services that exclude a resident. (2) Face-to-face medical exam within 60 days before or 30 days after admission, on AHCA Form 1823 or the practitioner's form. (3) Admission package contents, and what the resident receives at or before admission. (4) Continued residency: exam at least every 3 years or after a significant change, bedridden limit of 7 consecutive days, stage 2 sore conditions, and terminally ill/hospice retention.

citations.title: Resident Care Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Supervision and written record of significant changes. (2) Activities program (12 hrs/week, 6 days/week). (3) Arrangement for health care and transportation. (5) Bill of Rights posting, written grievance procedure, posted complaint numbers in 14-point type, house rules, no uncompensated work, telephone access. (6) Third-party services and 30-day communication. (7) Elopement standards. (8) Physical restraint care plan. (9) Assistive devices. (10) Infection control: hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection.

citations.title: Medication Practices
citations.requirement: Rules for self-administration, pill organizers, assistance with self-administration by trained unlicensed staff, and administration by licensed staff. Also CLIA certificate when facility staff perform lab tests, medication observation records, storage (locked, central storage triggers), disposal timelines, labeling and orders, and OTC/stock supply.

citations.title: Do Not Resuscitate Orders (DNROs)
citations.requirement: Written DNRO policies. A DNRO may not be required as a condition of admission. At admission, give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent) and DH Form 1896. Document in the record whether DH Form 1896 is executed. Honor an executed form. Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest.

citations.title: Staffing Standards
citations.requirement: (1) Administrator qualifications (21+, HS/GED, Level 2 screening, core training and competency test within 90 days), up to 3 facilities, managers appointed in writing, and notice of administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006. (2) Staff health statement within 30 days, annual TB documentation, Level 2 for staff and contracted staff, written contracts with staffing agencies. (3) Minimum weekly staff-hours table, awake overnight staff at 17+ residents, CPR/First Aid staff at all times, in-charge rules during administrator absence, written 24-hour schedule, AHCA authority to order more staff.

citations.title: Staff Training Requirements and Competency Test
citations.requirement: 26-hr core training plus competency test (75% to pass) within 3 months; 12 hrs CE every 2 years. 2-hr preservice orientation before resident contact. In-service training: infection control, adverse incidents and emergency procedures, resident rights and abuse, behavior and ADLs, safe food handling, elopement, HIV/AIDS. First Aid/CPR. 6-hr medication-assistance course with 2 hrs annual CE. Food service CE. ECC, LMH and ADRD training.

citations.title: Food Service Standards
citations.requirement: Written food service designee. USDA Dietary Guidelines-based menus, reviewed annually by a dietitian or nutritionist. Menus planned 1 week ahead, and menus as served kept 6 months. Therapeutic diets as ordered. Meal-interval limits. 3-day nonperishable food supply. County health department reports kept for 2 years. Contracted food service documentation.

citations.title: Fiscal Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: resident trust funds not co-mingled with facility funds (a single trust account is allowed with separate written accounting per resident) (2). Surety bond if the facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney (3). Liability insurance in force at all times, with proof filed at each renewal or policy change (4).

citations.title: Records
citations.requirement: Records must be readily available at the licensee's physical address. Lists required facility records, including the admission/discharge log, required policies, inspection reports, and the license on display. Also required staff records, resident records, retention (resident contracts 5 years; other resident records 2 years after departure), and inspection access.

citations.title: Resident Contracts
citations.requirement: Contract offered before or at admission with required provisions: services and rates, 30-day written notice of rate increases, deposits and refund policy, written bed hold policy, religious affiliation, transfer notice, 3-year assessment, medication and DNRO policies. Resident gets a copy. Additional charges need an itemized statement and a signed, dated addendum.

citations.title: Emergency Management
citations.requirement: Written CEMP on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023) covering the listed components. Annual submission and county emergency management approval, with significant modifications submitted within 30 days. Staff trained within 30 days of hire. Evacuation reporting within 6 hours. Emergency shelter above licensed capacity with a 48-hour report and a log.

citations.title: Emergency Environmental Control for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Plan to hold ambient temperature at or below 81°F for 96 hours after power loss. At least 20 net sq ft per resident, calculated on 80% of licensed beds. Fuel onsite: 48 hrs (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hrs (17+). Carbon monoxide alarm. Plan submitted before licensure. Proof of county approval sent to AHCA within 30 days. Written heat-injury mitigation procedures. Notice to residents within 5 business days.

citations.title: Inspection Responsibilities
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: county health department inspects sanitation, food hygiene and biomedical waste (1). Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects fire safety (2). AHCA inspects everything else (3).

citations.title: Physical Plant Standards
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: Florida Building Code and ch. 69A-40 fire standards (1)-(2). Resident furnishings (3): bed with mattress at least 36x72 inches, closet or wardrobe, dresser, nightstand or table, lamp, wastebasket. Facility keeps master keys, and provides linens and laundry service.

citations.title: Limited Mental Health
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LMH facility requirements, including a community living support plan and cooperative agreement per mental health resident. Records requirements cross-referenced in 59A-36.015(3)(r). Staffing cross-referenced in 59A-36.010(3)(f).

citations.title: Extended Congregate Care Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: ECC license requirements, including a nurse on staff or under contract, monthly nursing assessments, quarterly service plan review, adequate awake staff at all hours, and ECC admission/residency criteria and disclosure.

citations.title: Limited Nursing Services
citations.requirement: Per fact-checked research: LNS facility must employ or contract a nurse available as needed. Services require a practitioner's order. Monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes are kept.

citations.title: Licensing and Change of Ownership
citations.requirement: Licensure application and change-of-ownership procedures (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: License required; fee
citations.requirement: A license is required to operate an ALF (subsec. 1). Specialty licenses ECC and LNS (subsec. 3). Biennial fees (subsec. 4).

citations.title: Limited mental health license
citations.requirement: LMH license requirements and training for facilities serving mental health residents.

citations.title: Contracts
citations.requirement: Resident contract content and refund policy; implemented by Rule 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents
citations.requirement: Medical examination within 60 days before or 30 days after admission (subsec. 5). Hospice exceptions (subsec. 1). Disagreement on placement appropriateness (subsec. 8), as referenced in Rules 59A-36.006 and 59A-36.018.

citations.title: Use of personnel; emergency care
citations.requirement: Facilities with 17 or more beds must keep a working AED on the premises (subsec. 3(a)). The section also underpins the DNRO rule.

citations.title: Property and personal affairs of residents
citations.requirement: Surety bond when acting as representative payee or under a power of attorney (subsec. 2). Safekeeping of up to $500 cash and $500 in personal effects by mutual consent, and verified statements at least every 3 months (subsecs. 3-4), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Business practice; personnel records; liability insurance
citations.requirement: Records, personnel records and liability insurance (subsec. 3) requirements, per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Resident bill of rights
citations.requirement: Resident Bill of Rights, grievance and facility-procedure rights. It is cited in Rules 59A-36.007(5) and 59A-36.011 and in the fact-checked research. Section text was not independently re-fetched in this pass, so confirm subsection details before quoting them.

citations.title: Staff training and educational requirements
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for core training, 12-hour administrator CE (subsec. 5) and the medication-assistance training (subsec. 6).

citations.title: Background screening
citations.requirement: Level 2 background screening of owners, administrators and staff.

citations.title: Background screening; prohibited offenses
citations.requirement: Level 2 screening standards, with rescreening every 5 years (subsec. 2), per fact-checked research.

citations.title: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse
citations.requirement: Screening results are shared through the AHCA Clearinghouse (help line 850-412-4503 per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Long-term care managed care plan accountability
citations.requirement: SMMC LTC plans and ALFs negotiate rates. There is no state rate table.

citations.title: Health care licensing application procedures
citations.requirement: Online licensing and renewal filing. Per fact-checked research, renewals must be filed online (effective 3/5/2024).

citations.title: Florida minimum wage
citations.requirement: Minimum wage is $15.00/hr from Sept 30, 2026.

citations.title: Optional State Supplementation
citations.requirement: OSS base provider rate $991.40/month and $160 personal needs allowance (eff. 6/24/2025), per fact-checked research. DCF determines eligibility.

citations.title: Mandatory reporting of abuse, neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults
citations.requirement: Statutory duty to report to the Florida Abuse Hotline. NOT fetched and not in the provided research; confirm text before publication.

citations.title: Internal risk management and quality assurance; adverse incidents
citations.requirement: Adverse incident reporting to AHCA and internal risk management. NOT fetched and not in the provided research; confirm timelines before publication.

citations.title: Rules establishing standards (elopement drills)
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.007(7)(c) as the basis for documented elopement drills. Statute text NOT fetched; confirm drill frequency.

citations.title: Assistance with self-administration of medication
citations.requirement: Statutory basis for unlicensed assistance with self-administration (cited in Rules 59A-36.008 and .011). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Visitation policy
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.015(1)(v) as the basis for the required facility visitation policy. Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Notice of change of administrator
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.010(1)(e) (10-day notice). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Patients with Alzheimer's disease or other related disorders; certain disclosures
citations.requirement: Cited in Rules 59A-36.006(3)(a)13 and 59A-36.015(1)(h) (written description of special Alzheimer's services; keep advertisements). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Uniform Fire Safety Standards for Assisted Living Facilities
citations.requirement: Fire safety standards enforced by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal. Referenced in Rules 59A-36.005, .006, .010 and .014. Text NOT fetched. Confirm drill and inspection frequency.

citations.title: Community-based residential facilities (DOH sanitation)
citations.requirement: DOH sanitation and food hygiene standards for ALFs. Referenced in Rules 59A-36.012(3) and 59A-36.015(1)(l). Text NOT fetched.

citations.title: Maintenance of records; reports
citations.requirement: Cited in Rule 59A-36.015(1)(m) and (4)(b). AHCA survey, inspection and complaint reports and notices of sanctions are kept 5 years and made available to residents and the public. Statute text NOT fetched.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: Administrator: age 21+, HS diploma/GED, Level 2 screening; 26-hr core training and 75% competency test within 90 days (Rule 59A-36.010(1), .011)
One administrator may oversee up to 3 ALFs; a manager must be appointed in writing for each facility
Notify AHCA of an administrator change within 10 days on AHCA Form 3180-1006
Administrator CE: 12 hrs every 2 years
Written designation of who is in charge during administrator absence

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Policy Review and Regulatory Compliance
state_specifics: Do not admit residents before the license is issued (s. 429.07(1))
Do not represent services beyond the license type (standard/ECC/LNS/LMH)
Capacity changes need prior AHCA Central Office approval; converting uninspected space to resident use needs Field Office approval
Send annual fire and sanitation inspection copies to AHCA Central Office within 30 calendar days
License displayed; renewals filed online; written policies reviewed annually with a dated revision log

policies.title: Quality Assurance, Risk Management and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Internal risk management and adverse incident program under s. 429.23 (confirm timelines before publication)
Review incidents, grievances, falls, medication errors and elopements at least quarterly with the governing body
Track survey deficiencies and plans of correction
Staff trained on adverse incidents and emergency procedures within 30 days of hire

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
federal: 31 USC 3729 (False Claims Act, if billing Medicaid)
state_specifics: SMMC LTC plans negotiate rates with each ALF; no state rate table
OSS base provider rate $991.40/mo with $160 personal needs allowance (eff. 6/24/2025); third-party supplementation is voluntary
Identify state-funded residents to AHCA on request (Rule 59A-36.004(6))
Charge only for services in the contract or a signed addendum

policies.title: Liability Insurance, Workers' Compensation and Fiscal Standards
state_specifics: Liability insurance in force at all times; proof filed with AHCA at each renewal or policy change; no dollar minimum in rule
Certificate shows facility name, street address, ALF status, licensed capacity and dates
Workers' compensation required at 4+ employees (Ch. 440, F.S.)
Wages at or above FL minimum wage ($15.00/hr from 9/30/2026)
Resident trust funds never co-mingled with facility funds

policies.title: Resident Rights, Bill of Rights and House Rules
state_specifics: Post the Resident Bill of Rights (s. 429.28; Rule 59A-36.007(5))
House rules provided in writing before admission
No uncompensated work by residents; telephone access preserved
Residents may not be retaliated against for exercising rights
Confirm s. 429.28 subsection details before quoting

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
state_specifics: Written grievance procedure given to residents
Post complaint numbers (Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873, AHCA, Ombudsman) in 14-point type
Ombudsman and agency representatives have access to residents
AHCA Assisted Living Unit: (850) 412-4304, assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com
Document each grievance, investigation and response

policies.title: Admission Agreement (Resident Contract), Fees, Deposits and Refunds
state_specifics: Contract offered before or at admission; resident receives a copy
30-day written notice of rate increases
Must state deposits, refund policy, written bed hold policy, religious affiliation, transfer notice
Additional charges need an itemized statement and signed, dated addendum
Contract retained 5 years

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
state_specifics: Surety bond if facility is representative payee or holds power of attorney; copy filed with AHCA yearly
Safekeep up to $500 cash and $500 personal effects by mutual consent
Verified statement to each resident at least every 3 months
Separate written accounting per resident if a single trust account is used

policies.title: Advance Directives and Do Not Resuscitate Orders
federal: 42 CFR 489.102 (not applicable unless the facility participates as a Medicare/Medicaid provider type subject to it; confirm)
state_specifics: A DNRO may not be required as a condition of admission
At admission give Form SCHS-4-2006 (or equivalent) and DH Form 1896
Document in the record whether DH Form 1896 is executed; honor an executed form
Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest
Policy is part of the admission package (Rule 59A-36.006(3)(a)11; Ch. 765, F.S.)

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Records kept at the licensee's physical address and readily available to AHCA
Release of records only with authorization or as required by law
HIPAA applies if the facility is a covered entity; otherwise apply as confidentiality standard
Privacy for personal care, mail, telephone and visits

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Admit and retain by the criteria in Rule 59A-36.006 only
Provide interpreter or translated materials on request
Reasonable accommodations for disabilities

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
state_specifics: Resident must be 18+, able to perform ADLs with assistance, able to transfer with help
Not bedridden (except hospice); no stage 3-4 pressure sores
Administrator determines appropriateness based on the admission policy and services the facility can provide or arrange
Must not need 24-hour licensed mental health treatment
Admission policy and continued residency criteria given to the resident

policies.title: Admission Package and Required Disclosures
state_specifics: Give the package at or before admission with a signed receipt

Includes criteria, rates, personal care and nursing services with costs, diets, transportation, other services, activities, services arranged but not provided, house rules, DNRO/advance directive policy
Add ECC description, Alzheimer's special services description and elopement policy where applicable
Disclose any central medication storage rule (Rule 59A-36.008(6)(b)6)

policies.title: Resident Assessment, Medical Examination and Reassessment
state_specifics: Face-to-face medical exam on AHCA Form 1823 (or practitioner's form) within 60 days before or 30 days after admission
Exam at least every 3 years or after a significant change
Document significant changes in condition in the record
Record the practitioner's findings regarding the resident's ability to self-administer medication
Reassess after hospitalization or significant change

policies.title: Service Plan / Care Plan
state_specifics: ECC: quarterly service plan review and monthly nursing assessments
LNS: services require a practitioner's order; monthly nursing assessments and progress notes
LMH: community living support plan and cooperative agreement for each mental health resident
Involve the resident and representative in the plan
Physical restraint use requires a care plan (Rule 59A-36.007(8))

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
state_specifics: Bedridden limit of 7 consecutive days
Stage 2 pressure sore conditions limited per Rule 59A-36.006(4)
Terminally ill residents retained with hospice per rule conditions
Identify nursing services that exclude a resident under Rule 59A-36.006(1)
Exceptions only within the facility's licensed ECC/LNS scope

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
state_specifics: Transfer notice terms must appear in the resident contract
Placement disagreements handled under s. 429.26(8)
Follow Rule 59A-36.006(5) on discharge
Refund of deposits per contract and s. 429.24
Update admission/discharge log (Rule 59A-36.015)

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
state_specifics: Medications kept locked; follow labeling and order requirements
Central storage policy, if any, must be disclosed to the resident before admission
Follow disposal timelines in Rule 59A-36.008
Medication observation records maintained
CLIA certificate needed if staff perform lab tests

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
state_specifics: Unlicensed staff may only assist with self-administration after the 6-hr course (RN or pharmacist certificate) and with written informed consent
2 hrs annual medication assistance CE
Administration is by licensed nurses only
All trained staff must follow the infection control policy when assisting with medications
Pill organizers and self-administration per Rule 59A-36.008

policies.title: Nursing Services and Delegation (LNS)
state_specifics: LNS requires a nurse employed or contracted and available as needed
Nursing services only on a practitioner's order
Monthly nursing assessments and nursing progress notes
Nursing services provided must be described in the admission package with cost

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
state_specifics: Written record of significant changes (Rule 59A-36.007(1))
New exam after a significant change
Notify the resident's representative and practitioner
Arrange health care and transportation (Rule 59A-36.007(3))
Send DNRO form and records with transferring resident

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
state_specifics: If advertising special Alzheimer's care, provide a written description of those services (s. 429.177)
ADRD staff training per Rule 59A-36.011
Identify ADRD residents for emergency planning
Retain advertisements per Rule 59A-36.015(1)(h)

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Skin Integrity
state_specifics: Residents with stage 3-4 pressure sores cannot be admitted; stage 2 conditions limited per rule
Assistive devices per Rule 59A-36.007(9)
Document falls as incidents
Report significant changes in skin condition to the practitioner

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
state_specifics: Bedridden limit does not apply to hospice residents
Terminally ill retention on hospice per Rule 59A-36.006(4)
Third-party services arranged with 30-day communication (Rule 59A-36.007(6))
Hospice procedures take precedence in an arrest

policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: Honor executed DH Form 1896 as applicable
Notify representative and practitioner
Update the admission/discharge log
Retain records 2 years after departure

policies.title: Extended Congregate Care: Aging in Place, Residency Criteria, Services and Staffing
state_specifics: Applies only to facilities holding an ECC license
Nurse on staff or contracted; monthly nursing assessments; quarterly service plan review
Adequate awake staff at all hours
Admission package describes ECC residency criteria, added services, cost and room limits
ECC training: 4 hrs administrator/ECC supervisor (plus 4 hrs CE every 2 years), 2 hrs direct care staff

policies.title: Extended Congregate Care: Resident Choice and Participation
state_specifics: Residents take part in developing, reviewing and revising their service plan
Residents stay in the same room, except a move into the ECC section if only part of the facility is licensed
Residents select social and leisure activities
Facility arranges transportation to community activities on request
Residents may give input on adoption and amendment of facility policies; consult a family member or representative if help is needed

policies.title: Limited Mental Health Residents
state_specifics: LMH license required before admitting mental health residents; standard license and no uncorrected violations
Administrator and direct-contact staff: 6 hrs DCF-approved training within 6 months, then 3 hrs CE every 2 years
Community living support plan and cooperative agreement per resident
No extra AHCA fee for LMH

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Report to Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873 (confirm s. 415.1034 text before publication)
Post the hotline number
Staff trained in resident rights and abuse reporting within 30 days of hire (1 hr)
Level 2 screening of all staff before resident contact
Never retaliate against reporters

policies.title: Incident and Accident Reporting
state_specifics: Adverse incident reporting to AHCA under s. 429.23 (confirm timelines before publication)
Document every incident in the resident record
Notify practitioner and representative
Evacuation reporting separate: within 6 hours (Rule 59A-36.019(4))

policies.title: Elopement and Missing Resident
state_specifics: Elopement response policy given in the admission package
All staff trained within 30 days of hire and demonstrate competency
Documented elopement drills per Rule 59A-36.007(7)(c) (confirm frequency in s. 429.41(1)(k))
Identify residents at risk of elopement
Search and notification procedure, including law enforcement

policies.title: Restraints and Restrictive Practices
state_specifics: Any physical restraint requires a care plan (Rule 59A-36.007(8))
Restraint only as the rule permits and as ordered
Document use and monitoring
Prefer least restrictive alternatives

policies.title: Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP): All Hazards, Responsibilities and County Coordination
state_specifics: Use AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept 2023)
Submit to county emergency management each year and within 30 days of significant modification; county is final authority
Name staff responsible for each part of the plan
Post-disaster: family inquiries, medical intervention, transportation, report to county the number and location of relocated residents
All staff trained on the plan; new staff within 30 days of hire

policies.title: Care of Residents Sheltering in Place
state_specifics: Cover pre-disaster preparation and protecting the facility
Supplies, food and water, staffing and emergency equipment
Emergency power per Rule 59A-36.025
Emergency shelter above licensed capacity needs a 48-hour report and a log

policies.title: Evacuation of Residents
state_specifics: Identify residents to be evacuated; transfer records
Arrange transportation, sheltering, supplies, staffing, equipment and medications
Report any evacuation to county emergency management and AHCA within 6 hours of the order
Track resident location

policies.title: Receiving Evacuees from Other Facilities
state_specifics: Identify additional residents, staffing and supplies
Emergency shelter above licensed capacity: 48-hour report and a log
Record evacuee medications and conditions

policies.title: Residents with Alzheimer's/Related Disorders or Mobility Limitations: Specialized Assistance
state_specifics: Maintain a current list of ADRD and mobility-limited residents
Define assistance needed on-site and during evacuation
Update list at least with every plan submission and after changes in condition

policies.title: Emergency Environmental Control: Alternate Power, Fuel and Carbon Monoxide Alarm
state_specifics: Maintain 81°F or lower for 96 hours after loss of power
At least 20 net sq ft per resident, calculated on 80% of licensed beds
Fuel on site: 48 hrs (16 or fewer beds) or 72 hrs (17+ beds)
Contract for maintenance and testing of the generator
Carbon monoxide alarm; plan submitted before licensure; proof of county approval to AHCA within 30 days

policies.title: Heat-Injury Mitigation During a State of Emergency
state_specifics: Cooling devices and equipment
Refrigeration and freezers for ice and medication storage temperatures
Wellness checks for dehydration and heat injury
Medical intervention from emergency services when life safety is in jeopardy
Notice to residents within 5 business days (Rule 59A-36.025)

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation and Drills
state_specifics: Local fire authority or State Fire Marshal inspects annually under ch. 69A-40
Send inspection reports to AHCA within 30 days
Confirm drill frequency in ch. 69A-40 before publication
AED required at 17+ beds (s. 429.255(3)(a))
Facility keeps master keys to bedrooms

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Hand hygiene, standard precautions, equipment disinfection (Rule 59A-36.007(10))
1 hr infection control training before personal care
County health department inspects sanitation and biomedical waste
HIV/AIDS training within 30 days

policies.title: Smoking, Visitation and Pets
state_specifics: Written visitation policy required for the application and Rule 59A-36.015(1)(v) (s. 408.823)
Post visiting hours in house rules
Smoking areas per fire code
Pets per house rules

policies.title: Food Service and Therapeutic Diets
state_specifics: Written food service designee; menus reviewed annually by a dietitian or nutritionist
Menus planned 1 week ahead; menus as served kept 6 months
3-day supply of nonperishable food
County health department reports kept 2 years
Admission package states ability to accommodate special diets

policies.title: Activities and Social Programming
state_specifics: Activities program of 12 hours/week, 6 days/week
Residents choose activities
Include in the admission package

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry and Maintenance
state_specifics: Provide linens and laundry service
Resident furnishings per Rule 59A-36.014(3): 36x72 inch mattress, closet, dresser, nightstand, lamp, wastebasket
Maintain the premises in repair

policies.title: Transportation
state_specifics: Arrange transportation to health care (Rule 59A-36.007(3))
State availability and extra cost in contract
Arrange transportation to community activities on request (ECC)

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
state_specifics: Awake staff at all hours at 17+ residents
Staff member with First Aid/CPR on site at all times
Written 24-hour schedule; AHCA may order more staff
Maintenance, clerical and food-only staff hours do not count

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
state_specifics: Level 2 screening through the AHCA Clearinghouse for owners, administrator and staff including contracted staff
Rescreen every 5 years
Clearinghouse help line 850-412-4503
Written contracts with staffing agencies

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
state_specifics: 2-hr preservice orientation before resident contact
1 hr infection control before personal care
Within 30 days: 1 hr adverse incidents/emergencies, 1 hr resident rights and abuse, 3 hrs behavior/ADLs, elopement, HIV/AIDS
Medication assistance: 6 hrs plus 2 hrs annual CE
First Aid/CPR with skills demonstration

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
state_specifics: Staff health statement within 30 days of hire
Annual TB documentation
Retain in personnel file

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Keep screening, training, license and health records for each staff member
Training certificates and CE hours tracked
Available for AHCA inspection at the facility address

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No uncompensated work by residents
No misuse of resident funds or property
Pay at or above the Florida minimum wage ($15.00 from 9/30/2026)

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
state_specifics: Resident contracts retained 5 years
Other resident records retained 2 years after departure
Records available at the licensee's physical address
Admission/discharge log maintained

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Annual fire and sanitation reports to AHCA within 30 days of inspection
Administrator change within 10 days (AHCA Form 3180-1006)
Annual CEMP to county; evacuation within 6 hours
Renewal filed online at least 60 days before expiration
AHCA survey and complaint reports kept per Rule 59A-36.015

forms.name: Admission Package Receipt and Checklist
forms.purpose: Documents delivery of all Rule 59A-36.006(3) disclosures

forms.name: Resident Contract and Addendum for Additional Charges
forms.purpose: Contract per Rule 59A-36.018 with itemized charge addendum

required_items.text: Provision for all hazards;

Provision for the care of residents remaining in the facility during an emergency, including pre-disaster or emergency preparation; protecting the facility; supplies; emergency power; food and water; staffing; and emergency equipment;

Provision for the care of residents who must be evacuated from the facility during an emergency including identification of such residents and transfer of resident records; evacuation transportation; sheltering arrangements; supplies; staffing; emergency equipment; and medications;
Provision for the care of additional residents who may be evacuated to the facility during an emergency including the identification of such residents, staffing, and supplies;
Identification of residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, and residents with mobility limitations who may need specialized assistance either at the facility or in case of evacuation;
Identification of and coordination with the county emergency management agency;

Arrangement for post-disaster activities including responding to family inquiries, obtaining medical intervention for residents, transportation, and reporting to the county emergency management agency the number of residents who have been relocated, and the place of relocation; and,
The identification of staff responsible for implementing each part of the plan.
All staff must be trained in their duties and are responsible for implementing the emergency management plan. New staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of employment.

The acquisition of a sufficient alternate power source such as a generator(s), maintained at the assisted living facility, to ensure that ... ambient air temperatures will be maintained at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours in the event of the loss of primary electrical power. [The plan must include the area(s) where the temperature will be maintained, and the systems and equipment and fuel required to operate them.]

The acquisition of sufficient fuel, and safe maintenance of that fuel at the facility, to ensure that ... there is sufficient fuel available for the alternate power source to maintain ambient temperatures at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours ... The plan must include information regarding fuel source and fuel storage.

The acquisition of services necessary to maintain, and test the equipment and its functions to ensure the safe and sufficient operation of the alternate power source maintained at the assisted living facility.
The acquisition and maintenance of a carbon monoxide alarm.

Each assisted living facility shall develop and implement written policies and procedures to ensure that the assisted living facility can effectively and immediately activate, operate and maintain the alternate power source and any fuel required for the operation of the alternate power source. ... Procedures must address the care of residents occupying the facility during a declared state of emergency, specifically, a description of the methods to be used to mitigate the potential for heat related injury including:
The use of cooling devices and equipment;
The use of refrigeration and freezers to produce ice and appropriate temperatures for the maintenance of medicines requiring refrigeration;
Wellness checks by assisted living facility staff to monitor for signs of dehydration and heat injury; and
A provision for obtaining medical intervention from emergency services for residents whose life safety is in jeopardy.

The facility's admission policy and the services the facility is prepared to provide or arrange in order to meet resident needs. [Basis for the administrator's appropriateness-of-admission determination.]
The facility's admission and continued residency criteria;
The daily, weekly or monthly charge to reside in the facility and the services, supplies, and accommodations provided by the facility for that rate;
Personal care services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Nursing services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Food service and the ability of the facility to accommodate special diets;
The availability of transportation and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Any other special services that are provided by the facility and additional cost if any;
Social and leisure activities generally offered by the facility;
Any services that the facility does not provide but will arrange for the resident and additional cost, if any;
The facility rules and regulations that residents must follow as described in Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C.;
The facility policy concerning Do Not Resuscitate Orders pursuant to Section 429.255, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C., and Advance Directives pursuant to Chapter 765, F.S.;

If the facility is licensed to provide extended congregate care, the facility's residency criteria for residents receiving extended congregate care services. The facility must also provide a description of the additional personal, supportive, and nursing services provided by the facility including additional costs and any limitations on where extended congregate care residents may reside based on the policies and procedures described in Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C.;

If the facility advertises that it provides special care for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders, a written description of those special services as required in Section 429.177, F.S.; and,
The facility's resident elopement response policies and procedures.
All trained staff must adhere to the facility's infection control policy and procedures when assisting with the self-administration of medication.

The facility's rules and regulations require central storage of medication and that policy has been provided to the resident before admission as required in Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C. [Medication central-storage policy, if the facility has one.]
Aging in place; [ECC only: the facility must develop and implement specific written policies and procedures that address:]
The facility's residency criteria developed in accordance with the admission and discharge requirements described in subsection (4), and extended congregate care services listed in subsection (7);

The personal and supportive services the facility intends to provide, how the services will be provided, and the identification of staff positions to provide the services including their relationship to the facility;

The nursing services the facility intends to provide, identification of staff positions to provide nursing services, and the license status, duties, general working hours, and supervision of such staff;
Identifying potential unscheduled resident service needs and mechanisms for meeting those needs including the identification of resources to meet those needs;
A process for mediating conflicts among residents regarding choice of room or apartment and roommate; and,

How to involve residents in decisions concerning the resident. The services must provide opportunities and encouragement for the resident to make personal choices and decisions. If a resident needs assistance to make choices or decisions, a family member or other resident representative must be consulted. Choices must include at a minimum whether:
To participate in the process of developing, implementing, reviewing, and revising the resident's service plan,

To remain in the same room in the facility, except that a current resident transferring into an extended congregate care services may be required to move to the part of the facility licensed for extended congregate care, if only part of the facility is so licensed,
To select among social and leisure activities,
To participate in activities in the community. At a minimum the facility must arrange transportation to such activities if requested by the resident; and,
To provide input with respect to the adoption and amendment of facility policies and procedures.

sections: Rule 59A-36.019 - Emergency Management: (1) Emergency plan components (a)-(h); (2) Plan approval; (3) Plan implementation; (4) Facility evacuation; (5) Emergency shelter

official.notes: Florida publishes no single policy-and-procedure checklist for ALF licensure. The AHCA ALF page lists none, and the application is filed through the AHCA online licensing system. The items above therefore come from the rule sections that list written content. Every item is quoted from the Cornell LII copy of the F.A.C. text, whose notes show the amendment dates in each document's version field. Compare against the official Florida Administrative Rules Gateway (flrules.org) before relying on it. Organization and submission: (1) The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan must be written on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept. 2023) and submitted to the county emergency management agency, which is the final administrative authority. A significant modification must be submitted within 30 days (59A-36.019(2)). (2) The emergency power plan under 59A-36.025 supplements the CEMP. A new ALF must submit and implement it before obtaining a license. After county approval, proof of approval must go to AHCA at assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com within 30 days, along with a consumer-friendly summary. AHCA's page offers an Emergency Power Plan Sample Format. The written power policies (59A-36.025(5)) must be kept at the facility, be producible immediately, and be open to residents and their representatives. (3) The 59A-36.006(3) admission statement can be met with the resident contract or a brochure that contains all 14 items. Resident contracts must also meet Rule 59A-36.018, which was not fetched. (4) The ECC policies in 59A-36.021(2) apply only if the facility seeks an ECC license. They must be kept as a record under 59A-36.021(8)(d). LNS (59A-36.022) and LMH (59A-36.020) list no written policy topics. They set staffing, records, and per-resident plans. Not reviewed: Rules 59A-36.007 (facility rules and resident rights), 59A-36.009, 59A-36.010 (staffing), 59A-36.011 (training), 59A-36.012 to 59A-36.018, and ss. 429.28 and 429.41, F.S. These may require further written policies, such as rules and regulations, DNR, resident rights, and abuse reporting. Verify them against the rule text before finalizing the manual. The AHCA ALF survey tags PDF may also be useful, but it was not opened.
